new_statements.rule_in_words: The authors list 'loss of contrastive stress' as a phonological innovation shared by all Northeastern Luzon languages, of which Paranan is (tentatively) a member: i.e. the inherited Proto-Philippine accent contrast is said to have been lost, so stress is treated as non-contrastive. No placement rule is given anywhere in the article and there is no prose discussion of stress. Their own Paranan citation forms nevertheless carry acute accents on the final syllable in 72 of 91 distinct marked forms and on the penult in 19 (e.g. ágtaʔ, ápduʔ, dígus, dúwa, péklat, túglad), never earlier, so surface stress as they transcribed it is predominantly final but not uniformly so and is not obviously weight-conditioned (closed penults occur in both sets: ág.taʔ vs. bəŋ.ŋə́g, ap.pát).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the marked data include ~21% penult-accented forms, which the table's 'loss of contrastive stress' claim does not address.
new_statements.domain_note: Elicited citation forms (1,000-item wordlist and 100-200 sentences per variety, Sept-Oct 2006, via Tagalog). The claim is historical-comparative (a subgroup-defining innovation), not a synchronic description of Paranan word stress; the same table row covers Dupaningan, Pahanan, Dinapigue, Casiguran and Nagtipunan Agta.
new_statements.identity_note: Paranan [prf], glottocode para1306: the language of the non-Agta ('Palanenyo') residents of Palanan town, Isabela, distinct from the mutually intelligible Pahanan Agta [apf] (agta1234, 'Palanan Dumagat') spoken by the Agta of the same town; until ISO change request 2009-086 (effective 2010) both were under one code [agp] 'Paranan', which is why the SIL 1965 wordlist and 2012 fact sheet are filed as 'agp'. Robinson & Lobel 2013 collected their Paranan data in Palanan town in 2006 and treat Paranan as only a tentative member of Northeastern Luzon (Pahanan-like lexicon, divergent functors, non-Agta substratum, pp. 126, 128). The stress statement quoted is a subgroup-level claim, not specific to Paranan.
